# dsh-cc-computer-use-mcp

Wires a local cc-computer-use MCP server into DeepSeek Harness —
**one independent process per root

session**, so every session gets its own Xephyr sandbox screen and its own
private AT-SPI bus.

## Mounting follows the workspace MCP switch (since 2026-10-23)
These tools register in **each agent's own layer** (scope-local): the global lens cannot see them, s

o
`@local/dsh-mcp-workspace-policy`'s MCP menu used to omit this server entirely and `restrict` coul

d not hide
it. The two sides are now wired together:
- this plugin calls `declarePerAgent({ name })` on the policy service, so the menu lists `cc-compute

r-use`
with the same tool-count hint as any other server (the Host counts from the live sessions tha

t mounted it);
- **unchecked means not mounted** — no MCP process, no Xephyr, no AT-SPI bus (default

his plugin mounts or calls
`fiber.dispose()` for the live sessions in that workspace, so the child e

er version without the declaration API) it
**fails open** and mounts as before — a missing policy mu
st never take the user's tools away.
> ⚠️ After upgrading, check `cc-computer-use` in the MCP menu for every workspace that needs compute

r
> control. Default-off means unselected workspaces no longer get these tools.

On plugin hot-reload the old fiber is stored on
`agent[Symbol.for('dsh-cc-computer-use-mcp/mounted-f

iber')]`; the new instance adopts it and then keeps or
disposes it according to the latest selection

— otherwise a second process would be mounted and hit
mcp-client's `serverName` reservation error.
## Why one process per session
### The problem
A cc-computer-use sandbox is **one MCP server process = one Xephyr + one private AT-SPI bus**. It wa

s designed
around Claude Code's model (one MCP server child per session), but DSH's `@deepseek-ai/ds

h-mcp-client` is
mounted at **profile scope** (`scopeOf(ctx) ?? ctx.root`), so the whole dsh process

spawns exactly one server.
Every session therefore shared:

- the same Xephyr (one X11 pointer/keyboard focus),
- the same i3 window tree — a window A launched

with `launch_app` shows up in B's `list_windows`, and B's
`click` can land on A's window,
- the same

`RefTable` (ref numbers collide) and the same `ScreenLock` (one session holds it, the other is
refu

sed),
- the same private AT-SPI bus.
Two agents using it at once fight over the sandbox — the "they're stealing my sandbox" symptom.
### Why not several sandboxes in one process
That would use fewer processes, but it hits a hard libatspi constraint: `atspi_init()` is **process-

wide and
one-shot**, so a process can bind exactly one AT-SPI bus, and `exit` + re-`init` against an

other bus is known
to corrupt its internal state (see `_BUS_STALE_ERROR` in cc-computer-use's `backe

nd/linux/atspi.py`). Two
screens imply two buses, so **two screens require two processes**. This is

also cc-computer-use's own design
assumption.
### Why only root agents
A subagent is the same task's other hand and should work on the same screen (serialization is provid

ed by
cc-computer-use's screen lock). DSH's tool view inherits along the **scope ancestor chain**
(`
ToolRuntime.view` → `chainLayers`: the global layer plus every ancestor layer), so a subagent alread

y sees
the tools mounted by its parent and must not start another process — that would leave one san
ls mounted by its parent and must not start another process — that would leave one sandbox orphaned.

Three predicates identify a subagent; any one being true skips the mount: `agent.parentAgent`,
`sess
ion.header.origin === 'subagent'`, `session.header.delegationDepth > 0`.
### Lifecycle
`agent.ctx` is agent-local: "its contributions are agent-local, unwind on disposal". Closing a sessi

on unwinds
the plugin, which disconnects the MCP child, which exits and lets cc-computer-use's `atex

it` reclaim its
Xephyr. No orphan screens.
## Why the same `serverName` is safe
Tools register through `ctx.tools.register` as **scope-local**. DSH's own duplicate-name error spell

ugh `ctx.tools.register` as **scope-local**. DSH's own duplicate-name error spells out the
contract:
> `tool "X" is already registered (for a per-agent variant, register through that agent's agent.ctx
X" is already registered (for a per-agent variant, register through that agent's agent.ctx instead)`

The same reasoning holds for `systemPrompt.section` (a scoped section shadows a global one) and
`mcp
Resources.register` (layered by the calling scope), so many agents can share `cc-computer-use` witho

ut
colliding, and the model-facing tool names stay stable.
## Installation / new-environment notes

1. The cc-computer-use frozen artifact must exist at `config.command`
(`<cc-computer-use repo>/dist/

computer-use-mcp`). Re-run its `build.sh` after changing its source.
2. **This package needs `@deeps

eek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` to be resolvable.** Its `package.json` does not declare
it (profiles have no
`@deepseek-ai/*`), so a symlink provides it:
